tagline: Jinx's anthem: the song that turned Arcane's return blue.
headline: Ashnikko wrote Jinx's song, and Riot turned Paint The Town Blue into the battle cry of Arcane's final season.
summary: Released on September 5, 2024 alongside the official Arcane Season 2 trailer, Ashnikko's "Paint The Town Blue" was the first single from the final season's soundtrack and was written as Jinx's song. Riot named its award-winning Season 2 social campaign after it, Ashnikko gave the song its live debut before the Worlds 2024 final at London's O2 Arena, and the season's fourth episode shares its title. It now has about 169.5 million Spotify plays, and the trailer it launched with has 39.5 million views on League's YouTube channel alone.

story.heading: A fan writes Jinx's song
story.body:
Ashnikko already had a Riot credit before *Arcane* called. In 2022 the alt-pop artist fronted *Fire Again*, the VALORANT Champions anthem written with Grabbitz and Slinger, whose music video now sits at about 26.6 million views. For the final season of *Arcane*, the brief was far more personal: write a song for Jinx. Riot's global head of music Maria Egan told NME that Ashnikko is a huge fan of the show and especially of Jinx, and Ashnikko called *Arcane* their favourite show ever.

The result, written by Ashnikko (Ashton Nicole Casey) with Slinger, is a high-octane electronic track that runs just under two minutes. EUPHORIA read it as a look inside Jinx's psyche, a song about accepting the villain role everyone has already assigned her. Ashnikko told NME it is a sister song to *World Eater* from the 2023 debut album *WEEDKILLER*.

story.heading: Lead single, lead trailer
story.body:
On September 5, 2024, Riot premiered the official *Arcane* Season 2 trailer and released *Paint The Town Blue* the same day through Riot Games and Virgin Music Group, as the first single from the Season 2 soundtrack. The Line of Best Fit noted that the trailer was built around the track, and Riot's own chapter markers open it with "The fall of Jinx". On the League of Legends YouTube channel alone, that trailer has now been watched about 39.5 million times.

Ashnikko could barely contain it. The announcement on social media read "i wrote jinx's song for arcane season 2!!!!!!", and Ashnikko added that the first viewing of the trailer ended in an ugly cry in the street, calling the whole thing an actual dream come true and a career highlight.

story.heading: Painting the timeline blue
story.body:
Riot went further than a single. Its Season 2 social campaign with the agency We Are Social carried the song's title, and its "Paint The Town Blue" phase ran from August to October. A month-long scavenger hunt let fans unlock 21 songs from the Season 2 soundtrack, a daily "Arctober" challenge kept the community posting, and hundreds of Riot channels repainted their social profiles blue before fans were given the tools to do the same. By the entrants' count the campaign drew more than 450 million organic views and reached over 217 million accounts, and it won the Audience Honor in the Organic Promotion category at the 17th Shorty Awards.

Fans picked up the brush as well: TikTok even has a discover page titled "How to Do The Paint The Town Blue Trend".

story.heading: A live-action riot
story.body: On October 30, 2024, NME premiered the official music video, and Netflix posted it to its YouTube channel the same day. Maria Egan called it "our first live action music video inspired by the show". A defaced Jinx wanted poster opens the clip, then Ashnikko, in spiked blue hair, leads a crew of blue-haired followers through an industrial plant staffed by workers in red hazmat suits. The video has about 7.2 million views on Netflix's channel.

story.heading: Jinx takes the O2
story.body:
Three days later the song had its live debut on one of esports' biggest stages. Riot booked Ashnikko for the opening ceremony of the Worlds 2024 final at London's O2 Arena on November 2, alongside Mars Atlas of Forts and Tiffany Aris with *Still Here* and Linkin Park with the Worlds anthem *Heavy Is The Crown*. GosuGamers previewed the set as Ashnikko performing as Jinx, and that is what the arena got: spiked blue hair, a glowing grid stage filmed from overhead and a horde of dancers swarming around the singer.

The final that followed, T1 against Bilibili Gaming, peaked at 6.94 million concurrent viewers, which KitGuru, citing Esports Charts, reported as the most-watched match to date. The ceremony video on the League of Legends channel has about 8 million views.

story.heading: Inside the show
story.body:
When Season 2 arrived on Netflix in three acts starting November 9, the song became part of the story. The fourth episode, which opened Act II on November 16, is titled *Paint the Town Blue*. In it Piltover occupies Zaun to hunt Jinx while her blue-haired followers, the Jinxers, are arrested in large numbers, and Ashnikko's song is listed in the episode's music credits.

Streams followed the story. The song entered Spotify's daily global chart and peaked at No. 130 on November 25, two days after the final act landed, with top-50 daily peaks in Bulgaria, Poland, Estonia and France. The full Season 2 soundtrack passed 500 million streams in under three weeks, and in the UK *Paint The Town Blue* entered the Official Physical Singles Chart at No. 21 in December 2024.

story.heading: Still painting
story.body:
The song kept moving after the finale. On April 4, 2025, the Season 2 Extended Edition added a remix by producer BloodPop, released on the Riot Games Music channel with a visualizer of Jinx aiming a glowing blue weapon. In May 2025 the Season 2 soundtrack the song had launched won Favorite Soundtrack at the American Music Awards, ahead of *Wicked*, *Moana 2*, *Hazbin Hotel* and *Twisters*. That autumn the single returned to the UK Official Physical Singles Chart and climbed to a new peak of No. 13 on October 2, 2025.

Today the original single has about 169.5 million plays on Spotify, making it Ashnikko's fourth most-streamed song there, behind *Daisy*, *Slumber Party* and *STUPID*. For League and *Arcane* fans the legacy is simpler: the final season's first single, its social campaign, an episode title and a live Jinx at Worlds all trace back to one Ashnikko song.

whyItMatters: It was written as Jinx's song for Arcane's final season and was the first single fans heard from the Season 2 soundtrack.
Riot and We Are Social named their Season 2 social campaign after it; the campaign drew 450M+ organic views and won a Shorty Awards Audience Honor.
It launched alongside the official Season 2 trailer, which has about 39.5M views on the League of Legends YouTube channel alone.
Ashnikko gave it its live debut at the Worlds 2024 final opening ceremony in London, ahead of the most-watched esports match to date (6.94M peak viewers).
Season 2's fourth episode shares its title, tying the song directly to Jinx and her blue-haired Jinxers.
It reached Spotify's daily global chart (No. 130), has about 169.5M Spotify plays and peaked at No. 13 on the UK physical singles chart.
It brought Ashnikko back to Riot after VALORANT's Fire Again (2022), again writing with Slinger.
